rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 7 (base_speed 1.6, outer sensors at y = 0.05, inner at y = 0.03, kd 0.5, kp 3.0, ki 0.05) is the best raced design at 219.96, with 6 of 20 oval completions. Iteration 8 raised base_speed to 1.8 and scored 136.1. Oval completions fell to 0 (progress 0.645), s-bend progress fell to 0.236, and slalom progress was 0.114. Every run ended off_track, so speed 1.8 is past the point where bends are survivable. Line loss stayed near 1.0 per run on every track, as it has in every raced iteration. The approved entityR1 for 1.8 was written before it raced, and its own revert rule (s-bend progress below 0.30) has now fired. The revert rule also says to test controller.ki at 0.15 next, since line loss has stayed near 1.0 through every geometry, kp, kd and speed change.

Change. Revert controller.base_speed to 1.6. Test controller.ki at 0.15 (from 0.05). Geometry and all other gains are identical to iteration 7, so the result reads directly against 219.96 and the only variable changed is ki. The integral term is limited to ±2, so with ki 0.15 it adds at most about 0.3 to turn, small next to kp*signal, which is why I expect it to be a gentle change rather than a destabiliser.

Hypotheses. (a) A somewhat larger integral term corrects the small steady offset that builds on the long bends, so line-loss events fall below about 0.9 per run on the s-bend and slalom. (b) If line loss stays at about 1.0, the cause is turn-in lag or sensing coverage at bend entry, not steady offset, and the next lever is a forward sensor offset further than y = 0.05 or a line_loss behaviour change.

Expected result. Score at or above about 215, with oval completions at 5 or more and progress held (oval about 0.76, s-bend about 0.36). Risk: a larger integral can overshoot after a bend and raise max_error. Revert rule: if oval progress falls below 0.70 or s-bend progress falls below 0.30, return ki to 0.05 and keep base_speed 1.6.

Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and noise_robustness on each track, so the ki effect on line loss and off-track endings can be separated.
